Alphabet uses the operational control approach to define its organizational boundary for GHG emissions accounting.
Alphabet accounts for all emissions from operations over which it has operational control, including data centers, offices, and other assets.

Category 1 (Purchased goods and services) includes upstream emissions from manufacturing consumer devices and spare parts, Alphabet's food program, and additional goods and services purchased for operations.

We calculate electricity procured from renewable sources (%) on an annual basis by dividing the megawatt-hours of renewable electricity procured by the total megawatt-hours of electricity consumed by our global operations.
Renewable electricity procured includes contractual instruments, on-site renewable electricity generation, and renewable electricity in the electric grids where our facilities are located.

To achieve our 100% renewable energy match, we first consider both our on-site renewable electricity generation and the renewable electricity already in the electric grids where our facilities are located.
We then procure renewable electricity through contractual instruments to achieve our 100% renewable energy match.

Alphabet utilizes the operational control approach, as defined by the GHG Protocol, to establish relevant operations for emissions, energy, and water metrics at Alphabet's owned and leased data centers, offices, and other assets.
Alphabet uses a 25-year estimated lifespan for solar panels in both annual and lifetime emissions reduction methods.
